storyboard.addedInformation: The coin in his hand prices the ruinous rate the narration only describes.
storyboard.claim: The ruinous rate compounded into memory interest that dwarfed it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jason holding the trip photo over the paid-off debt coins: the suicide rate that compounded into memory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the loan-shark setup: naming the price of the $10,000 trip.

storyboard.addedInformation: The cascade shows memories compounding past the financial interest the narration compares them to.
storyboard.claim: The memory interest on the trip beat the loan shark's financial interest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jason holding the trip photo beside the paid-off debt coins: the financial interest dwarfed by memory interest.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast to the ruinous rate: a higher compounding curve wins.

storyboard.addedInformation: The strike says the money is refused, not counted — the narration only says he would not trade.
storyboard.claim: Jason survived the debt and would not trade the trip for any money today.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jason waving off a coin: decades of dividends no payout can buy back.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the compounding: the debt is gone, the memory is not for sale.

storyboard.addedInformation: The trekking body shows what $10 million cannot repurchase — youth itself.
storyboard.claim: No fortune at 50 can repurchase a hostel-and-Alps youth trip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Young Jason trekking with a heavy pack among backpackers, a trip age alone permits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why he would not trade: the experience is unreplicable at any price.

storyboard.addedInformation: The spent hourglass shows the closed window the narration declares shut.
storyboard.claim: The biological window for that trip closed forever; he cashed in before it did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Jason walking on as the last sand falls: the window he slipped through in time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism behind unreplicability: the window shut.

storyboard.addedInformation: The scale stages the two risks side by side so the viewer weighs them, not just hears them.
storyboard.claim: Missing the memory compounding was the greater risk, not the debt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A scale weighing coins against memories, tipping toward the memories.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The verdict on Jason's gamble: reframed through temporal economics.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the open logistical question the narration poses before Perkins answers it.
storyboard.claim: Frontloading life raises a logistical nightmare: how to organize it all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host laying out the organizing problem: a lifetime to frontload, no system yet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the radical example to the practical objection it provokes.

storyboard.addedInformation: The entry-level desk shows the constraints — job, salary, limits — the narration lists.
storyboard.claim: You cannot do everything at 25: jobs and entry-level salaries constrain you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman at a junior desk with a briefcase: willing, but bound by salary and schedule.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The constraints that make the organizing system necessary.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names Perkins's system as the answer to the logistical challenge just raised.
storyboard.claim: Time buckets replace the depressing terminal bucket list.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins sweeping a terminal bucket list aside, pointing at life buckets instead.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The answer arrives: a system to replace the bucket list.

storyboard.addedInformation: The panicked scribble shows the midlife-crisis list the narration mocks.
storyboard.claim: The bucket list is a panicked reactive scribble from a midlife crisis or health scare.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped, frantically scribbling a last-minute list on a notepad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What time buckets replace: the desperate napkin list.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins's pointing posture marks the turn from reactive to proactive the narration argues.
storyboard.claim: Bucket lists fail because they are biologically impossible by the time you write them — be proactive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins pointing forward: plan the experiences while the body can still do them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rejection hardens into the prescription: proactivity.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages capability as falling steps, not the flat plateau the narration denies.
storyboard.claim: Human life is not a straight unending plateau of capability — hence 5-to-10-year buckets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host gesturing along a capability curve that steps downward by decade.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The premise that justifies bucketing: capability declines.

storyboard.addedInformation: Sorts the lifespan into the three named windows the narration defines.
storyboard.claim: Life divides into three health windows: go-go, slow-go, and no-go years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three successive life windows, capability falling left to right.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The system formalized: the three buckets everything maps onto.

storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass in hand makes the invisible expiry date visible and countable.
storyboard.claim: Every experience carries an invisible expiry date set by physiology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman studying an hourglass: each dream stamped with a date he cannot see.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stakes of the three windows: everything in them expires.

storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the three pools side by side so the analogy lands without water iconography.
storyboard.claim: Life is a resort with three pools: kiddie, teen slide, and serene senior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three pools side by side — calm kiddie water, a towering slide, a still senior pool.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The analogy that makes the buckets concrete: pick the pool for your age.

storyboard.addedInformation: The older figure turned from the slide shows the refusal and its irreversibility.
storyboard.claim: Skip the teen pool while teen and you cannot return to it at 65.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An older visitor seated before the tall slide he saved himself for and now cannot ride.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The analogy's warning: the skipped pool stays skipped.

storyboard.addedInformation: The seated body — not a wallet — carries the claim that wealth cannot override physiology.
storyboard.claim: No riches at 65 override the lifeguard and the body: the slide is unrideable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wealthy older visitor refused at the slide: money intact, body unable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why return is impossible: the constraint is flesh, not finance.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host's hushed delivery bridges the analogy to the book's quietest tragedy.
storyboard.claim: These windows close quietly — the book's most tragic illustration follows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host lowering his voice: the saddest proof of silent expiry is next.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From analogy to evidence: how silently closure really happens.

storyboard.addedInformation: The worn DVD is the ritual object the narration centers the memory on.
storyboard.claim: Perkins's weekend ritual: a worn Heffalump DVD watched with his daughter, pure magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A father in medium shot holding up the scuffed DVD, weekends of magic in a photo-keepsake.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tragic illustration begins: the ritual before it breaks.

storyboard.addedInformation: The shrug against the father's outstretched DVD stages the asymmetry the narration describes.
storyboard.claim: One day the 10-year-old just shrugs at the ritual and looks back at her screen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The father offering the DVD while his daughter shrugs, eyes on her screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The ritual breaks: the shrug that ends years of magic.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slump carries the unfelt snap the narration says arrives without signal.
storyboard.claim: The window snapped shut without warning — no signal, just gone.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The father slumped on the couch, DVD in lap, the magic ended mid-silence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The meaning of the shrug: closure arrived unannounced.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins's pointing turns grief into method: match each adventure to its bucket.
storyboard.claim: Stop assuming next weekend: ruthlessly map adventures to the bucket where bodies still work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins in medium shot pinning each adventure onto a living heart: dreams mapped to the able years.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lesson of the shrug: schedule by biology, not hope.

storyboard.addedInformation: The mid-30s skier embodies converting cash to memory inside the open window.
storyboard.claim: Convert money to memory before windows close: ski Japan's backcountry at 35.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A skier carving deep powder in his prime window, spending youth while it spends well.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The prescription in action: the right adventure in the right bucket.

storyboard.addedInformation: The young believer shows why timing is the gift — belief itself expires.
storyboard.claim: The Disney trip works at 8, when the princess is real — never at 18.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A parent watching the childhood clock run out: belief has an expiry date.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same rule, second proof: childhood magic has its own bucket.

storyboard.addedInformation: The empty-handed sitter shows departures that announce nothing — no device in frame.
storyboard.claim: No phone alert announces the last hide-and-seek: things depart without notice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A parent holding a phone with no notification, the kid grown past the game: the absence is the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The general law behind both stories: endings send no notification.

storyboard.addedInformation: The pushback staged through the host keeps the objection live before it is answered.
storyboard.claim: The pushback: bucketing life into five-year declining spreadsheets sounds bleak.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host challenging the system: a life reduced to a spreadsheet of decline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The system meets resistance: is this planning or morbidity?

storyboard.addedInformation: The Sunday planner with his ledger embodies the decay-scheduling the narration winces at.
storyboard.claim: It feels like a Sunday spent scheduling our own decay and obsolescence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman at a desk on Sunday, ledgering his own decline in five-year rows.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection sharpened: we are mapping our obsolescence.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slump concedes the feeling honestly before the rebuttal reframes it.
storyboard.claim: Mapping physical obsolescence feels morbid at first glance — admitted.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped under the weight of his own mapped decline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The concession: yes, it feels morbid — first glance granted.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host's level delivery reframes: the schedule describes decay, it does not cause it.
storyboard.claim: The brain resists decay, but decay proceeds whether scheduled or not.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host steady-handed: the decline continues with or without your spreadsheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rebuttal begins: ignoring decay does not pause it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The averted gaze shows self-blinding, not stopped time — the negation staged as loss.
storyboard.claim: Refusing to acknowledge time blinds you to passing opportunity; it stops nothing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman looking away from the falling sand: covered eyes, open hourglass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cost of denial: blindness, not immunity.

storyboard.addedInformation: Perkins's forward point turns finitude into fuel, the mechanism the narration names.
storyboard.claim: It is deliberate aggressive maximization: finitude creates the urgency to live now.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins pointing at the present moment: the finite window as a starting gun.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The reframe complete: not decay-mapping but urgency-making.

storyboard.addedInformation: The booked ticket in hand shows what two remaining summers do that forever never does.
storyboard.claim: Forever means next year means never; two summers left means booking today.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman booking the Italy tickets on his phone: two summers left, zero deferral.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Urgency demonstrated: scarcity books what abundance postpones.

storyboard.addedInformation: The dusk cemetery hill behind the host grounds mortality as meaning's source.
storyboard.claim: Mortality creates meaning: convert the cache to memory before the window boards up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host before a dusk horizon: the deadline that gives every plan its weight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The section's epitaph: death's deadline is the point.

storyboard.addedInformation: The recap posture closes the buckets argument before the funding problem opens.
storyboard.claim: Buckets established: frontload experiences and map them to healthspans.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host closing the first ledger: the mapping system settled, next problem pending.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Checkpoint: the what and when are solved; the how remains.

storyboard.addedInformation: The worried calculator shows the math wall the narration crashes into.
storyboard.claim: The math wall: how to fund a front-loaded life without going broke by 50.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman staring at accounts that must fund decades of frontloaded living.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The turn: from scheduling dreams to paying for them.

storyboard.addedInformation: The host's widened stance previews the book's most explosive claim without defusing it.
storyboard.claim: The book's most controversial economic concept is next.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host bracing the viewer: the rule-breaking idea lands in one beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The drumroll: the funding answer will break orthodoxy.

storyboard.addedInformation: The peak marked as a target shows the planned crest the narration introduces.
storyboard.claim: Peak net worth and the drawdown: Perkins sledgehammers retirement planning.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins marking the crest of a wealth curve: the summit you plan to descend.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The controversy named: peak, then deliberately fall.

storyboard.addedInformation: The suited foil's rising gesture embodies the always-up orthodoxy the narration quotes.
storyboard.claim: Orthodoxy: wealth should climb and compound until the day your heart stops.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wealthy adviser tracing an ever-rising chart: up and right, forever.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The old creed stated: die on the summit.

storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the summit the foil just traced — the creed quoted only to be broken.
storyboard.claim: Dying on the financial summit is a structural failure, not a triumph.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins striking through the ever-rising chart: the summit crossed out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The creed demolished: the summit is the failure.

storyboard.addedInformation: The long descending road shows the deliberate fall the narration commands.
storyboard.claim: Fortunes should crest around middle age, then deliberately fall toward zero.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Perkins tracing a wealth road that rises, crests, and deliberately descends.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The new law: accumulate, then de-accumulate — on purpose.
